questions.q: Why can't a plain foreign key express a many-to-many relationship?
options: A single foreign key column can only point to one row on the other side — it can't let both sides reference many rows of each other
Foreign keys are only allowed on primary key columns
SQL Server has a hard limit of one foreign key per table
Many-to-many relationships don't actually exist in relational databases
questions.explain: Expressing both sides referencing many rows of the other requires an intermediate table, not a single foreign key.

questions.q: What is a junction table (also called a bridge or linking table)?
options: A table sitting between two others, holding a foreign key to each, used to express a many-to-many relationship
A table that stores only primary keys with no other data
A temporary table used only during a transaction
A view that combines two tables' columns
questions.explain: Sales.SalesOrderHeaderSalesReason is a real example, connecting orders to reasons with no purpose beyond linking them.

questions.q: What does the junction table's primary key usually consist of?
options: A composite of both foreign key columns together
A single new IDENTITY column unrelated to either side
It has no primary key at all
Only the foreign key to the 'larger' of the two tables
questions.explain: The composite of both foreign keys enforces referential integrity in both directions and prevents duplicate pairs.

questions.q: In AdventureWorks2012, what does Sales.SalesOrderHeaderSalesReason represent?
options: The many-to-many link between sales orders and the sales reasons that applied to them
A one-to-one relationship between orders and customers
A list of every possible sales reason with no connection to orders
A backup copy of SalesOrderHeader
questions.explain: One order can have multiple reasons, and one reason can apply to many orders — the classic many-to-many shape.

questions.q: Why does the junction table's composite primary key prevent duplicate pairs?
options: Because a primary key value can never repeat, the exact same (order, reason) combination can only be recorded once
Because it automatically deletes duplicate rows on a schedule
Because SQL Server rejects any junction table with more than one row
It doesn't prevent duplicates — that requires a separate CHECK constraint
questions.explain: Since the primary key is the pair of both foreign keys, inserting the same pair twice violates the primary key constraint.
